paper.title: Analysis of Thompson Sampling for Combinatorial Multi-armed Bandit with Probabilistically Triggered Arms

settings.name_in_paper: CMAB with probabilistically triggered arms (CMAB-PTA), semi-bandit feedback
unmapped: Base arm outcomes mutually independent (D = D_1 x ... x D_m), outcomes in [0,1]
Expected reward r(S, mu) depends only on S and mean vector; Lipschitz in l1 norm over triggering set with constant B (no monotonicity assumed)
Learner knows the problem structure (feasible super arms, triggering function, reward function) and has an exact computation oracle; only D unknown
settings.definition_quote: In short, the tuple $([m], {\cal I}, D, D^{\text{trig}}, R)$ constitutes a CMAB-PTA problem instance. Among the elements of this tuple only $D$ is unknown to the learner.

bound.regime: for all rho in (0,1) and 0 < eps <= 1/sqrt(e) with Delta_S > 2B(k_tilde^2+2)eps for all suboptimal S

symbols.L_lip: Lipschitz constant B of the expected reward in l1 norm (Assumption 3)
symbols.p_i: minimum nonzero triggering probability of base arm i
symbols.F_i: max over suboptimal S with i in triggering set of |S_tilde|/(Delta_S - 2B(k_tilde^2+2)eps)
symbols.K_tilde: maximum triggering set size over super arms
symbols.k_tilde: size of triggering set of optimal super arm S* with minimal triggering set

conditions: Expected reward depends only on S and mu (Assumption 2)
Expected reward Lipschitz in l1 norm over triggering set with constant B (Assumption 3)

source.label: t:gapdependent
source.quote: Under Assumptions \ref{a:independence}, \ref{a:rdependence} and \ref{a:rsmoothness}, for all $D$, the regret of CTS by round $T$ is bounded as follows: ... for all $\rho\in(0,1)$, and for all $0 < \varepsilon\leq 1/\sqrt{e}$ such that $\forall S\in\mathcal{I}-\text{OPT}$, $\Delta_S>2B(\tilde{k}^{*2}+2)\varepsilon$, where $B$ is the Lipschitz constant ..., $\alpha >0$ is a problem independent constant ..., and $\tilde{K} := \max_{S\in\mathcal{I}}|\tilde{S}|$ is the maximum triggering set size among all super arms.

results.notes: Regret defined via expected reward gaps, so pseudo-regret. CTS does not use T, so anytime. Abstract summarises as O(sum_i log T/(p_i Delta_i)). The max over S was folded into the declared per-arm symbol F_i. Paper's m (number of base arms) is renamed m_base because canonical m means something else.
